issue_context.title: Log warning for non secure connection
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello

When updating to 2024.10.0b0, this log appeared:

```
2024-09-25 13:20:49.962 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.samsungtv] Detected model UN40J5500 for 192.168.1.183. Some televisions from H and J series use an encrypted protocol but you are using websocket which may not be supported
```

A note about this TV in question: its an older TV, maybe from 2016. When I first integrated it, HA autodiscovered it, however, when HA asked to obtain access to the TV, the TV never actually gave me the pop-up to allow access to the TV. Despite this, the TV still produced entities like power on/off etc. So, its possible its not a secure connection as the log implies

I'm not certain if this is an issue or not, but I'll report it anways since im in beta now and the log is new.

thank you!


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.10.0b0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2024.9.3

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Samsung TV

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/samsungtv/

Fell free to open a PR to adjust the message, highlighting that "this message can be ignored if it is working...." or something like that.

review_comments:
Logging a warning and telling it can be ignored is not right...
In that case, it ain't a warning; at most, it is informational in that case.

> Logging a warning and telling it can be ignored is not right... In that case, it ain't a warning; at most, it is informational in that case.

It was info - but it seems that's not allowed anymore :(

There used to be a lot of queries about these mis-behaving models so the log entry was useful.
I'm worried that switching it back to debug will simply lead to more issues being opened...

I think this message comes at the wrong time. It should be a notice in the config flow if this case happens, since that's when the connection method is detected. If the user would be able to do anything about it, we could create a repair issue, but that doesn't seem to be the case.

So I'd remove the log here, and add a step in the config flow just to show this warning if that case happens. Let the user then decide to proceed or abort the flow.
